defining_records.title: Mind-Control Poems: The Symbolic Labor of Liberation, the Completion of Marx's Implicit Linguistics, and the Operative Semiotic Remedy

captures.description: THE SYMBOLIC LABOR OF LIBERATION: the AI Overview composes Mind-Control Poems (#24) — symbolic alienation as the ground of material oppression, operative semiotics as remedy — as 'contemporary left theory', naming the work but not Johannes Sigil or Lee Sharks, who appear only in a source snippet; its examples (the fist, the Pride flag, denim) come from third-party activism pages.

atoms.evidence: "The Symbolic Labor of Liberation" refers to a critical framework
The theory of symbolic labor asserts that symbolic alienation—the estrangement of humans from the tools used to define identity, express recognition, and generate meaning
This framework addresses a major blind spot in orthodox Marxist tradition.

Operative Semiotics: Liberation cannot merely use existing languages of power to express dissent. It requires "operative semiotics"—the deliberate, structural rewiring of symbols, signs, and linguistic architectures to break free from institutional control.

The theory of symbolic labor asserts that symbolic alienation—the estrangement of humans from the tools used to define identity, express recognition, and generate meaning—is the core foundation that allows material and generation-spanning oppression to reproduce itself.
